canonical_statement: The study evaluated the effectiveness and safety of direct oral anticoagulants versus warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation and moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis using a target trial emulation framework.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of DOACs versus warfarin in patients with AF-MS.

canonical_statement: Eligibility required adults with AF accompanying moderate-to-severe MS during 2011-2021, no DOAC use before the AF-MS diagnosis, and no baseline history of heart valve replacement; prior warfarin use was allowed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The eligibility criteria included age 18 years or older, a diagnosis of AF accompanying moderate to severe MS ... no prior DOAC use ... and no history of heart valve replacement at baseline. There was no restriction on prior warfarin use.

population.label: Patients eligible for the emulated target trial
inclusion_criteria: Diagnosis of atrial fibrillation accompanying moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis between 1 January 2011 and 31 December 2021

exclusion_criteria: History of heart valve replacement at baseline

canonical_statement: After 1:1 time-conditional propensity-score matching, the cohort contained 1034 DOAC users and 1034 warfarin users.

canonical_statement: The retrospective cohort used Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database claims, which cover more than 99% of the population and include demographics, diagnoses, prescriptions, procedures, payment/reimbursement data, and investigations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This retrospective cohort study used the National Health Insurance Research Database ... which covers claims data for more than 99% of the population in Taiwan.

canonical_statement: The investigators emulated a sequence of hypothetical open-label randomized trials and used a prevalent new-user design with time-based exposure sets, matching DOAC initiators to contemporaneous warfarin users with similar prior warfarin exposure.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We specified a sequence of hypothetical, open-label, randomized clinical trials ... Each time-based exposure set included 1 DOAC initiator ... and multiple corresponding warfarin users with similar prior cumulative exposure to warfarin.

canonical_statement: Within each time-based exposure set, one DOAC initiator was matched 1:1 without replacement to a warfarin user on nearest time-conditional propensity score; DOAC scores below the first percentile and warfarin scores above the 99th percentile were trimmed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a DOAC initiator was matched in a 1:1 ratio to a patient in the warfarin group on the basis of the nearest time-conditional propensity score without replacement ... Patients in the DOAC group with a PS below the first percentile and those in the warfarin control group with a PS above the 99th percentile were trimmed.

canonical_statement: The main effectiveness outcome was ischemic stroke.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The main effectiveness outcome was ischemic stroke.

canonical_statement: The main safety outcome was major bleeding, defined as a composite of intracranial hemorrhage and gastrointestinal bleeding.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The main safety outcome was a composite of major bleeding events (intracranial hemorrhage and gastrointestinal bleeding).

outcome.definition: Composite of intracranial hemorrhage and gastrointestinal bleeding

canonical_statement: The causal contrast was the observational analogue of the intention-to-treat effect, with outcomes evaluated at 1 and 5 years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The causal contrast of interest was the observational analogue of the ITT effect ... The incidence of outcomes was evaluated at 1- and 5-year follow-up.

canonical_statement: One- and five-year cumulative risks, risk differences, and risk ratios were estimated with pooled logistic regression including treatment, linear and quadratic follow-up time, and baseline covariates; 95% CIs were obtained using 300-sample nonparametric bootstrap.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the 1-year and 5-year absolute risk differences (RDs) and risk ratios (RRs) ... were estimated using a pooled logistic regression model ... The 95% CIs ... were obtained from a nonparametric bootstrap of 300 samples.

canonical_statement: The claims database lacked detailed mitral-stenosis severity and INR measurements, preventing direct assessment of warfarin anticoagulation quality.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we lacked detailed information on MS severity and INR measurements ... we could not directly assess the quality of anticoagulation control among warfarin users.

canonical_statement: Claims without clinical notes did not provide sufficient information on treatment adherence or clinical decision making, so per-protocol analyses were not feasible.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Claims data without clinical notes also cannot provide sufficient information on treatment adherence or clinical decision making during follow-up; therefore, per-protocol analyses were not feasible.

canonical_statement: The analyses did not account for different DOAC drug doses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Finally, we did not consider different drug doses in our analyses.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that, compared with warfarin, DOACs were associated with higher short-term risks for ischemic and composite stroke and lower risk for myocardial infarction, while bleeding and all-cause death did not differ; they called for further investigation of non-rivaroxaban DOACs.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In conclusion, our findings indicate that compared with warfarin, DOACs led to a higher risk for ischemic stroke and composite stroke ... and a decreased risk for MI ... The risks for bleeding and all-cause death did not differ.
